newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slip back amid quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slip back amid quiet trade.

text.p: Irish bonds slipped back in light early trade in line with other European markets, with a quiet session anticipated, dealers said.

"It's a quiet day for data and we're at the end of what's been a good week for the yield curve, so a slight decline won't be surprising," one dealer said. "On top of that we're still not really clear of the recent bearish phase."
Negative factors in the market included the overnight revising downwards of the U.S. trade deficit, which could push up GDP and have a negative effect on bonds, dealers said.
Hawkish comments about inflation pressures by Fed officials overnight and growing rumours about the possibility of an early French election were also playing on market nerves.
Irish PPI figures due at 1100 GMT, while not market-moving data, would be of interest, dealers said.
"In the past these numbers have been market-supportive - this time around it will be interesting to see if the fall of the punt against sterling has had any effect."
Meanwhile, M4 figures from the UK at 0830 GMT would be scrutinised for more signs of strong lending, dealers said.

By 0800 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 10 pence from Thursday's close at 102.10 to yield 5.95 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down 25 pence from the close at 108.75 to yield 6.70 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 140 basis points over Germany in the five-year area and 88 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area, a widening of two basis points on the close.
